title: The Rock Just Walked Out of the Ocean — and This Time, You Can See His Face
excerpt: Disney's live-action Moana sails into Indian theatres July 10 with Dwayne Johnson back as Maui, a brand-new wayfinder, and a Lin-Manuel Miranda song that puts both Moanas together for the first time.
body:
There is a moment in the trailer for Disney's live-action **Moana** where **Dwayne Johnson** steps out of the surf as **Maui**, chest tattoos glinting, fishhook slung over one massive shoulder, and grins like a man who knows exactly how good this looks. He does. The internet agrees. And on July 10, Indian audiences will get to see it on the biggest screen they can find.

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=-NN2q4OYCgE</youtube>

The original animated *Moana* was a sensation — a Pacific Island wayfinding epic that made $643 million worldwide in 2016 and then quietly became the most-streamed title in Disney+ history. Its sequel, *Moana 2*, added another $1.1 billion last year, turning the franchise into a $1.7 billion behemoth. Now Disney is doing what Disney does: remaking it in live-action, with real waves, real islands, and a very real Dwayne Johnson replacing his own voice performance.

Directed by **Thomas Kail** — the man who staged *Hamilton* on Broadway — the live-action *Moana* introduces **Catherine Laga'aia** as the new wayfinder. The Samoan-Australian actress, making her feature debut, steps into the role originated by **Auliʻi Cravalho**, who voiced Moana across both animated films. Cravalho hasn't been sidelined, though. In one of the remake's smartest moves, **Lin-Manuel Miranda** has written a brand-new original song called **"Along the Way"** that features *both* Moana actresses singing together — a passing-of-the-torch moment that bridges the animated legacy with whatever comes next.

> "Auliʻi and Catherine's voices blend so beautifully, and writing for Dwayne as Maui is just pure fun. I'm grateful that we were able to create something special for this brand-new version of our wayfinder's story." — Lin-Manuel Miranda

Miranda, who wrote the original film's earworm anthems *How Far I'll Go* and *You're Welcome*, returns as both songwriter and producer. The musical DNA is intact.

## Why This One Might Actually Work

Disney's live-action remakes have a credibility problem, and everyone knows it. *The Lion King* (2019) made $1.6 billion but felt like a screensaver. *Snow White* was a disaster. *Pinocchio* was forgettable before it finished streaming. The track record is wildly uneven, and audiences have grown skeptical of the "same movie but realistic" formula.

*Moana* has a few things working in its favour. The story is set in ancient Polynesia — lush, oceanic, visually spectacular in a way that benefits from real-world cinematography rather than CGI facsimile. The original's charm came from character, not photorealistic animals trying to emote. And casting Dwayne Johnson in a role where he gets to be physically massive, charming, and funny is less a creative gamble than a cheat code.

Kail's *Hamilton* background also suggests a director who understands rhythm, movement, and how to make a musical number land with physical bodies in physical space — exactly the skill set a live-action *Moana* needs.

## The India Play

The film releases in India on **July 10** in both **English and Hindi**, positioning it as the family counterweight to a July slate dominated by action and comedy. It opens the same week as **Dhamaal 4** and **Evil Dead Burn** — neither of which is competing for the same audience.

Johnson's pull in India is formidable and specific. Before he was a $20-million-per-film Hollywood star, he was **The Rock** — the most electrifying man in sports entertainment, watched by millions of Indian millennials during WWE's late-'90s boom. That generation now has children of the exact age to drag their parents to a Moana screening. Disney knows this. The Hindi dub isn't an afterthought; it's a strategic play for Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities where dubbed Hollywood family films have historically overperformed.

Just last week, Johnson showed up unannounced at a London school event alongside co-star Laga'aia, surprising children who had sent him a viral video invitation. It was the kind of moment — cameras catching genuine screaming kids — that plays beautifully on Instagram reels and reinforces exactly why studios keep handing this man franchises.

https://www.instagram.com/reel/DaSf30sBaIZ/

## The Bottom Line

At 120 minutes, directed by a Tony-winning stage director, anchored by a movie star with crossover appeal that stretches from Mumbai multiplexes to small-town single screens, *Moana* is the rare Disney live-action remake arriving with more goodwill than skepticism. The $1.7 billion franchise doesn't need to prove the story works. It just needs to prove the format does.

And if it doesn't? Well, there's always *Dhamaal 4* the same weekend. The ocean isn't going anywhere.
